title: Good back day Vs Bad back day
summary: He lays out his back-day philosophy: open with a hip hinge from the floor, follow with pull-ups and legless rows, finish with yoke and isolation work, and treat the back day as a leg day in disguise. He contrasts this with the bro-split back day of many lat pulldown variations, which he calls low-quality junk volume, and gives templates in the description.
claims: The upper back is the least developed area in natural lifters and the one with the most untapped growth potential
Do not treat the back as one muscle; it needs several movement patterns: hip hinges, vertical pulls and horizontal pulls
The hip hinge takes priority because it develops the whole posterior chain plus the upper back, so always open the back day with a pull from the floor; any deadlift variation or a rack pull works
The opening pull doubles as a warm-up; you are a bodybuilder, so do not burn out on it or the session becomes a lower-body day
He usually avoids a second hip hinge on the back day, though on gentleman splits, where the back day is also a lower day, hinges appear more often
The pull-up is the best mass builder for the upper back, especially the lats; since doing them religiously the difference has been night and day
Pull-ups barely tax the cardiovascular system, so superset them with forearm, ab or other small-muscle work
Use lat pulldowns only if you cannot do pull-ups yet or as a supplementary variation to change torso angle; never open a back day with pulldowns, they are not intense enough
A back day that never uses the legs is a failure; a natural's lower body can be trained 3-4 times a week, and skipping this leads to undersized legs
After the heavy pull, choose follow-up lifts that are gentler on the lower back

Rows from the floor load the lower back like a deadlift; touch-and-go rows with knee flexion are really a hip hinge, which is why people get lower back pain when they treat rows as a pure horizontal pull
If you love rows, replace deadlifts with rows one week out of two; it will not hurt your deadlift or upper back
Later in the workout use legless rows such as seal rows, dumbbell rows, weighted inverted ring rows or reduced-range rack rows
The upper back can take massive punishment and grow very big, but it is always limited by the lower back, so find ways to load it without the legs
Pull-ups deload the lower back and stretch the spine, and done properly they cause no overuse injuries
Finish the back day with isolation such as shrugs, rear delt work or rhomboid-focused pulls
The bad back day: a lat pulldown followed by five or six more pulldown variations is redundant junk volume; 3-4 sets of one heavy vertical pull already covers it
Pro bodybuilders and steroid users build the yoke with drugs; naturals should do shrugs with heavy loading, the stretch and partials on top of heavy floor pulls
Superset leg raises with pull-ups or rows on the back day to decompress the spine
Tonnage quality matters: machine circuits give diffuse, low-quality tonnage, while heavy deadlifts plus heavy compounds build a much thicker back
The deadlift grows the mid back most because the weighted stretch happens with the torso at about 45 degrees; he never needed a special mid-back exercise
A back day is a leg day in disguise: it should still hit the posterior chain, though less than a proper leg day
Bad back day example: lat pulldowns 3x10, pronated pulldowns 4x15, cable rows 4x10, single-arm cable rows 4x15, light dumbbell shrugs 4x20 with 3 min rests gives only a pump and some soreness
Good back day example: deadlifts 1x5 or 3x3, weighted pull-ups 3x5 or 3x3, dumbbell or seal rows 4x12, shrugs or high pulls 4x15

Back day template: heavy pull 1x5 or 3x3 (3x6-10 for RDL or row variations); vertical calisthenic pull 3x3 or 3x5 weighted or AMRAP bodyweight; horizontal pull 4x8-12 or a second hinge; yoke 4x10-15, a legless row, or hyperextensions/GHR/reverse hypers
exercises: any variation; opening lift; don't burn out
trains whole posterior chain and mid back via weighted stretch at 45 degrees
valid substitute for pulls from the floor
bodyweight or weighted; superset with small muscles
best upper back and lat mass builder; decompresses spine
use as variation to change torso angle, not as opener
only if you can't do pull-ups yet or as a supplement
touch-and-go with knee flexion is a hip hinge
can replace deadlifts every other week; loads lower back
upper back work without lower back load
reduced range, no deep knee and hip flexion
